verdicts.reasoning: Six of the ten stems hand the learner a fraction already set in notation and ask for its spoken word name, which is exactly the reading half of this competency. Two of them even open with the imperative 'Read the fraction', and the rest ask how it 'is read in words' or which word name represents it.

verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The distractor spelling 'halfs' appears in four option sets (seeds 11, 42, 91, 118); the plural of half is 'halves', and 'four halfs'/'three halfs' put a misspelling in front of a Grade 2 reader. Seed 57 also offers '8 oneths', which is not a word name at all.

verdicts.reasoning: Four seeds run in the opposite direction from the reading items: a word name is given and the learner must produce the notated form, with keys 3/5, 2/3, 4/5 and 2/3. The stem verb is literally 'Write ... in fraction notation', and deciding which numeral goes above and which below the bar is the skill this clause names.

verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The production is done by picking from four choices rather than by typing, so numerator/denominator order is cued by the option list (e.g. seed 23 offers both 3/5 and 5/3). Acceptable as a selected-response proxy, but no seed makes the learner construct the notation unaided.

verdicts.reasoning: Similar fractions are fractions that share a denominator, so exhibiting the term takes at least two fractions with a common bottom number in play. Every one of these ten stems presents a single isolated fraction instead - 2/4, 3/5, 2/5, 1/8, 2/3, 4/5, 3/4 - and the denominators across the batch are four, five, eight and three, never gathered into a same-denominator family. Nor do the option sets supply one: seed 91 mixes fourths, halves and thirds, and seed 118 mixes thirds and halves. Nothing here puts similarity between fractions in front of the learner.
